## Independent review of PR #168 (axis fit tightened band)

I reviewed `axis_robust.rs` statically and probed it with throwaway lib tests in a temp worktree, since removed. Nothing was pushed. The PR's own `axis_robust` lib tests pass. On exact meshes the change does what it says: `shaft + near-meridian strip` reads exactly, f32-rounded copies at X0 and X37.3 do too, and a keyed shaft (f32, X37.3) goes from 0.058 mm (plain) to 9e-8 mm.

**Verdict: 2 BLOCKING items.** Both come from the tightened band being driven by the median miss once the mesh is not exact. That is every real STL that has been through a tessellator, a decimator or a repair tool.

### BLOCKING 1: on noisy meshes the tightening can land further from the axis than the plain fit, and still reports `trusted`
Probe: `shaft(0)` (D20, z -30..30) plus the PR's own near-meridian strip, with a deterministic radial vertex jitter of amplitude `amp`. The "worst" proxy is the axis offset plus 30 mm × lean.

| case | robust (this PR) | plain (= main's result: every facet is inside the 3 % band) |
|---|---|---|
| jitter 1e-3 mm + strip | off 1.07e-3 mm, lean 4.6e-5 rad, worst ~2.45e-3, trusted, share 4.1 % | off 3.4e-4, worst ~7.8e-4 |
| jitter 5e-4 + strip | worst ~3.7e-4 | ~7.5e-4 |
| jitter 2e-3 + strip | worst ~1.1e-4 | ~8.3e-4 |
| jitter 1e-3, no strip | worst ~5.5e-5 | ~5.2e-5 |

A sweep over jitter 2e-4..1.7e-2 mm and strip widths 0.1..0.5 mm (196 cases) made the result worse than the plain fit in 34. The worst excess was jitter 1.48e-2 with strip 0.3: robust 6.3e-3 against plain 2.9e-3, trusted. The response is not monotone (5e-4 good, 1e-3 bad, 2e-3 good). The likely cause is that trimming on |residual| at 4× the median, then re-shrinking the band on the trimmed set, selects facets by their noise sign around a biased estimate. That gives the sign-selection bias that trimmed least squares is known for, and the refine step then turns it into a lean.

On the lathe, the spindle law (0.0005 mm) refuses these cases, so it is a wrong refusal and not a gouge there. Any consumer of `axis::fit` with no micron check (the rotary kinds) silently takes an axis a few microns worse than main's. This is the case the review was asked to hunt: a tightened band converging on a wrong axis that still passes every gate. The `judge` gate cannot catch it, because it works at the 3 % band.

Suggested direction (not prescriptive):
- Accept a tightened refit only if it does not raise a noise-robust residual of the coarse inlier set, for example its area-weighted median miss about the new axis against the settled one.
- Or tighten once, from a robust scale (about 3 × 1.4826 × MAD) of the coarse inliers, instead of re-shrinking from the trimmed set.

Pin it with a jittered-mesh test, for example the strip with 1e-3 mm jitter, asserting that robust is no worse than plain.

### BLOCKING 2: false "set aside" note on plain round bars
`outlier_share` is now measured against the tight band, so noise facets count as features. On main, every case below reports 0.
- An f32-rounded plain shaft at X1234.5 (a mill-turn import far from the origin) reads `outlier_share` = 5.6 %.
- Any jittered plain shaft (1e-5..1e-2 mm) reads 4.2 %.

Both are far above `NOTE_FLOOR` (0.05 %). `set_aside_note` then tells the user "5.6% of the turned surface (keyways, flats, holes, eccentric sections) was set aside and is not turned - machine those features in a later setup" about a bar that has no features. That is a wrong diagnostic on the most common part.

Fix: report the share against the coarse `REL_TOL` band about the final axis. The tight band's drop-outs are noise, not features, so they should not be named as such.

### Non-blocking
1. **The all-inliers branch can turn a trusted part into an untrusted one.** If `settle` fails after the first tightening (the `keep.iter().all` path), the code returns `as_is(share, false)`. Main returns `as_is(0.0, true)` there. I could not build a failing case (the median guarantees that ≥ 50 % of the area is kept at the start), but after a refit and re-trim `MIN_KEPT_SHARE` or `judge` can still fail. The comment's promise, "the last trusted fit stands", should hold there too: return `as_is(0.0, true)` on `Err` in that branch.
2. **Minimum inliers and coverage are kept.** Every tightened refit goes back through `settle`: at least 8 non-pole rows, at least 50 % of the answering area, and the full `judge` (90 % of the area inside 3 %, bearing-gap gate) on ALL facets. So a line can't be fitted through a handful of facets. On exact meshes the 1e-9·r floor leaves a large margin (misses ~1e-15 against a band of 1e-8).
3. **Hex bar with a turned pin:** fine. A flat's facets centred on its mid-meridian meet the axis exactly and stay in. Fanned flats miss by a large share of the flat's width and were outliers already. **Eccentric feature:** with the main body holding more than about 80 % of the area, the tightening snaps onto it (an improvement). Between 50 and 80 % it behaves like main.
4. **NaN and panics:** clean. `median_miss` filters out non-finite values, `tight_band` cannot go below 1e-12, the sort uses `total_cmp`, there is no `unwrap`, and the loops are bounded (4 × 4).
5. **Determinism (#151):** for exact meshes the margins are wide enough to be platform-stable. For noisy meshes, the chaotic response in item 1 combines with `sym_eigen`'s libm `atan2`/`cos`/`sin` (`linalg.rs:45-46`), whose last bits can differ on macOS. A one-ulp change in the eigen direction can flip which facets the tight band keeps, so the axis can differ by microns between platforms. Fixing BLOCKING 1 (a non-recursive band, accepted only on improvement) also removes most of this risk.
6. **Test coverage:** all the new pins use exact f64 meshes. Add at least one f32 or jittered case for both BLOCKING items.

Not approved, not merged. Static review plus a probe run of `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib -- axis_robust`.

Review findings addressed in cb4c497 (with a merge of origin/main, 254bbec, carrying #135).

**BLOCKING 1 (noisy meshes fitting worse than plain):** the tightening now runs ONCE. Its band is 5 sigma, with sigma the MAD scale (1.4826 x median miss) of the coarse inliers. There is one refit with no re-trim, and it is taken only if it passes every gate and lowers the coarse inliers' clipped residual. The sweep found a second cause, in code main already has: past ~15 um of jitter the 3 % sagitta band itself sits inside the noise (5 sigma ~ 0.75 mm), so the wide trim cut noise tails one-sidedly. The wide band is now max(3 % radius, 5 sigma of every facet's miss about the plain fit), and the wide trim is also taken only when it lowers the clipped residual. On exact meshes the band is unchanged from main.
Pin: `axis_robust::tests::a_noisy_shaft_with_a_strip_never_fits_worse_than_plain`, a 32-case sweep (jitter 0.2-17 um x strip 0.1-0.5 mm, ~0.1 s). Every case is no worse than plain. 1 um + strip reads 1.8e-4 against plain 7.0e-4; 14.8 um + strip 0.3 now equals plain (2.6e-3).

**BLOCKING 2 (false set-aside note):** `outlier_share` is read at the wide band.
Pin: `a_noisy_plain_shaft_sets_nothing_aside` (jitter 1e-5..1e-2 mm, and an f32 shaft at X1234.5), all at 0.

**Non-blocking 1:** taken. A declined tightening keeps the wide fit, trusted.
Tests moved to `axis_robust_tests.rs` (400-line law).

Re-run: motion multiaxis lib 38/38. lathe_cross_drill 5/5 (the one-hole pin passes). drilling_cross, _box, _part, _rapids, _spindle, _stock all green. lathe_spindle_fit, _keyed, _law green. drill_reach and drill_reach_fit green. Clippy on motion and app with all targets: clean.

## Re-review of PR #168 at cb4c497: clean

I re-ran the same throwaway probes as in the first review on this head and on `origin/main`, in temp worktrees that are now removed. Nothing was pushed. `axis_robust` lib tests: 7/7 pass.

**BLOCKING 1 (noisy meshes fitting worse than plain): resolved.**
The sweep is the same as before: `shaft(0)` with a near-meridian strip, radial jitter from 2e-4 to 1.7e-2 mm, strip widths 0.1 to 0.5 mm, 196 cases. "Worst" is the axis offset plus 30 mm × lean.

| | cases worse than plain | worst excess |
|---|---|---|
| previous head 076c77a | 34 | 3.4e-3 mm (6.3e-3 vs 2.9e-3) |
| `origin/main` | 10 | 3.4e-3 mm (the wide-trim cause the author found) |
| **cb4c497** | **2** | **1.8e-6 mm** (8.00e-5 vs 7.82e-5, share 0, jitter 1.54e-3, strip 0.1) |

The two remaining cases are within 2 nm of plain. That comes from the acceptance metric (clipped residual) not being the same quantity as my worst proxy. It is negligible, and the head is better than main in every case.

**BLOCKING 2 (false set-aside note): resolved.**
A jittered plain bar (1e-5 to 1e-2 mm) and f32 plain bars at X0, X37.3, X1234.5 and X5000 all read `outlier_share` = 0 and trusted, and the axis equals plain bit for bit.

**Regression check on the 5σ-widened wide band.**
I ran keyed shafts at 40 sizes: wall half-width 1 to 8 segments, floor x from 9.8 to 6, each exact, f32 at X37.3, and with 1e-3 jitter. The results are identical to `origin/main`; the only difference is one last-bit change (5.2163204829703e-5 against ...05214e-5). Feature walls still fall outside the widened band, and robust offsets stay at about 1e-7 mm (f32) to 2e-4 mm (jitter), against plain drags of 0.005 to 0.32 mm.

**Code.**
- The tightening is one pass, with no re-trim, and is taken only when every gate passes and the clipped residual drops. A declined tightening keeps the wide fit trusted, which settles my earlier non-blocking item 1.
- The minimum-row, minimum-area and full-judgement backstops still apply to every refit.
- No unwrap, panic or NaN path: `unwrap_or(false)` on `get`, non-finite misses filtered, `total_cmp` sort.
- Determinism: the remaining cross-platform sensitivity is a strict `<` between two clipped residuals. A one-ulp flip there picks between two fits that are nanometres apart, so it is no longer a #151-class risk.

No blocking items. Not approved, not merged.

**Estimated agent cost:** ~$1.15 (rough estimate from size: 495 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
